Letter From David Herrick; In Jail 1 Year;
Another Reason Why Something Has To Be Done To Implement Prop 215

May 18, 1998

365 Days in Actual Physical custody !!!
Happy Anniversary!

Well, we didn’t do as well as we thought we would, but there is always appeal. See

Orange County Cannabis Co-op Volunteer David Herrick Guilty on Two Counts Of "Selling"

My Defense Attorney Sharon Petrosino came and saw me today, and even though my max is 5 years in State Prison, she feels that the judge will either give me 1 or 2 years in county jail which I already have plus some.

365 Days in Actual Physical custody !!!
Happy Anniversary!

Well, we didn’t do as well as we thought we would, but there is always appeal. See

By my sentencing date June 26th, I will have a total of 404 actual days in custody plus credit for good & work time (202) for a total of 606 days. So if he gives me 2 years that will be a "Turn Around" and if he gives me a year that will be time off my probation.

Sharon Petrosino is requesting that Co-op members and supporters send letters to her, addressed to her, but made out to "Probation Officer". We need them within the next 4 weeks.

Please send letters to :
Sharon Petrocino, Dep. Public Defender, 901 Civic Drive, Suite 200, Santa Ana, CA 92703

I would like to thank Andrea Nagy (Ventura), Ellen Komp (215 Reporter) and Gene Weeks (Adelanto) who drove many miles to attend my trial, and would like their addresses so I can thank them personally. I also want to thank everyone else that has shown up in court or otherwise been supportive.

I was chained to Marvin when he appeared in court on Tuesday, so we got to talk for a while.

Until I talk to you again, be good, and thanks for everything.

Dave

P.S.

The following is a letter from a friend of Herrick’s

Dear Probation Officer,

I met David Herrick as a volunteer for the Orange County Cannabis Co-op. He was very helpful to me by providing information on the benefits of medicinal cannabis.

Shortly after meeting Dave, A close friend named Gil Linsay was diagnosed with terminal cancer and was given 6 months to live. Cannabis helped to ease his suffering by countering the effects of chemo., various medications and made it easier to sleep.

He was too ill to grow any for himself, and too poor to buy from the black market.

As a caregiver, I was unable to grow or acquire for him but I knew that Marvin Chavez and Dave were providing cannabis to persons in need who had a doctor’s letter of recommendation. After his oncologist at UCLA signed his letter he became a member and for a short time was able to receive the cannabis at a safe location at low (to no) cost.

It was so frustrating to sit and watch my friend suffer and to see the relief that he experienced through his use of cannabis was proof to me that Marvin and Dave were performing a valuable service to people who live with illness, disability and chronic pain. I don’t know where I would have gone or what I would have done without the help that they were able to provide for me and my friend Gil.

William Britt
